title: English File Upper-Intermediate, File 6: used to, be used to, get used to; gerunds and infinitives

fixIt.text: I'm not used to drive on the left.
fixIt.explain: be used to + -ing = it is normal for me.

fixIt.text: It took me months to get used to live alone.
She used to living in Battambang, but now she lives in Phnom Penh.
fixIt.explain: used to + verb: a past state.

fixIt.text: I remember visit Angkor Wat when I was six.
fixIt.explain: remember + -ing = remember something in the past.

fixIt.text: Don't forget locking the door when you leave.
fixIt.explain: forget + to + verb = something you must do.

fixIt.text: He stopped smoke five years ago.
fixIt.explain: stop + -ing = not do it any more.

fixIt.text: We can't afford buying a car this year.
I'm looking forward to see you.
fixIt.explain: look forward to + -ing (to is a preposition here).

builder.text: I'm used to the noise now.
builder.tip: be used to + noun: normal for me.

builder.text: I look forward to meeting you.

radio.title: Getting used to a new city
radio.text: When I first moved to Phnom Penh, I wasn't used to the traffic, and I was afraid of crossing the road. I used to live in a quiet village where everybody walked or cycled. It took me a year to get used to living with so much noise. Now I remember to carry an umbrella in the rainy season, and I have stopped worrying about the traffic. I still miss waking up to the sound of birds.
